messages:
mira: FYI AcmeHealth reported they suddenly started getting 403s when calling embeddings and rerank with their SSO-provisioned service key. They say nothing changed on their side. Error payload attached.

acme-support: (from customer) we call both endpoints using the same service key and started seeing failures for embeddings + rerank today. generation still works. please advise.

mira: Repro steps from customer (sanitized):
```bash
# embeddings call
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.prod.acme123\" \
  -d '{"input":"foo"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

# rerank call
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.prod.acme123\" \
  -d '{"candidate_documents":["a","b"],"query":"q"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
```

Response (embeddings):
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "missing_scopes": ["embeddings:write"]
}

Response (rerank):
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "missing_scopes": ["rerank:run"]
}

mira: They also tried creating a fresh API key from their SSO admin console (same flows we use) and it produced the same result. Generation endpoints (inference) continue to work.

joel: thanks — pinging @samir and infra-bot. quick theory: provisioning flow may have generated a service key that only includes the legacy inference scope. provisioning code path sometimes drops embed/rerank scopes when an org flag is set.

samir: can you paste the org id and a sample request id (if available)? I want to check the provisioning logs. also, do we have the provisioning job id that created the key?

mira: Org: org-acme-001, sample request id from their failed call: req_0b7c9f. provisioning job id not provided by customer yet — asking.

infra-bot: [provisioning] found last service-key creation for org-acme-001: job=prov-20260215-88, template=service-key-v2, scopes=[inference:generate,metrics:read] (this is internal metadata)

samir: that log is the smoking gun — template only had inference+metrics. rerank/embeddings scopes missing. Looks like the template selected was v2 which intentionally excludes embeddings/rerank for lower-priv team templates. we need to confirm why customer was routed to that template.

joel: short term workaround: create a new org-level service key using admin console with explicit scopes: `inference:generate`, `embeddings:write`, `rerank:run` and rotate in their app. Mira, can CS run through that with them?

mira: sending steps to customer now. quick note for the playbook I'm sharing:

1) Admin console -> Keys -> Create service key -> check boxes for:
   - inference:generate
   - embeddings:write
   - rerank:run
2) Replace key in app and test embeddings + rerank (no downtime required, just key rotation)
3) If rotation isn't possible, request a scoped temporary key from CS for repro.

acme-support: confirmed — followed the steps and both endpoints succeed now. thanks! :tada:

samir: great. root cause next steps:
- platform: audit template selection logic that maps org attributes -> key template (joel)
- eng: add a provisioning telemetry check that emits missing_scopes alarm when a created key lacks expected endpoint scopes (samir)
- cs: update runbook and include the rotation playbook (mira)

joel: I'll own the template mapping audit. initial hypothesis: org-acme-001 still has a legacy flag `restrict_high_priv_keys=true` which previously prevented creation of keys with rerank/embeddings. we changed policy last quarter but forgot to backfill some orgs. plan is to add a migration job to re-evaluate flagged orgs.

samir: I'll add a quick metric and a one-off job to scan recently-created keys and detect missing scopes for orgs that have used those endpoints (shouldn't be many).

mira: CS will follow up with AcmeHealth and keep this thread updated.

Action items (owners):
- joel (platform): audit template mapping + schedule org migration job (ETA 2 days)
- samir (eng): telemetry + key-scan job + PR for alarm (ETA 3 days)
- mira (CS): customer rotation confirmation + update runbook (ETA today)

mira: marking resolved for the customer since rotation fixed it, leaving thread open until platform patches template logic. :thumbsup:
